title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen Arrives, ChatGPT Gets a Wallet and More
summary: Today's AI news in simple words: Google's fast new Gemini 4 Hydrogen, ChatGPT Wallet for AI shopping, a Rs 49 lakh deepfake scam and Claude for factories.
intro: Happy Saturday! Today we look at a faster Gemini model you may already be using, a new way for ChatGPT to pay for things, and an important scam warning to share with your family.

news.headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast everyday model
news.body: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12. It is a quick, low-cost member of the Gemini 4 family and replaces Gemini 3.8 Flash as Google's everyday model. Free Gemini app users cannot pick it directly, but the app may use it automatically when a question needs it. People on paid plans like Google AI Plus and AI Pro can choose it. It is also becoming the default model behind AI Mode in Google Search, and developers can try it in the Gemini API, including the free tier.
news.why: You may notice faster and smarter answers in Gemini and Google Search without paying anything. Students building small apps can test it free in Google AI Studio.

news.headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet so AI agents can pay for you
news.body: OpenAI has launched ChatGPT Wallet, built with Visa, Mastercard and American Express. The idea is simple: you save your card once inside ChatGPT. Later, when ChatGPT's agent finds something to buy for you, like a product or a booking, it asks you to approve the purchase. You do not need to type your card details again each time. Every purchase still needs your approval. The reports do not say when, or if, it will come to India.
news.why: AI that shops for you is coming fast. Small online sellers should keep product details, prices and policies clear on their websites so AI agents can read them. As a user, never approve a payment you did not ask for.

news.headline: Fake AI video of the Finance Minister cost a Kerala woman Rs 49.2 lakh
news.body: A 45-year-old woman from Kozhikode, Kerala saw a Facebook video that seemed to show Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman praising an online trading platform with high returns. The video was fake. She clicked its link, followed the scammers' instructions and sent Rs 49.2 lakh to several bank accounts between July and September. The promised profits never came. Kozhikode Rural Cyber Crime Police registered a case on November 11 and are trying to trace and freeze the accounts.
news.why: Famous faces in an ad do not prove anything, because AI can fake them easily. If you or a family member is cheated online, call 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in as quickly as possible.

news.headline: Anthropic launches Claude for Manufacturing
news.body: Anthropic has released Claude for Manufacturing, a plugin with 17 ready-made skills for factory work. It can help prepare price quotes, investigate quality problems, write production reports, diagnose maintenance issues and help with sourcing. It reads a company's existing records and connects to tools like Microsoft 365, Oracle NetSuite, Infor and Autodesk Fusion. It does not control machines. For now it is for Claude Team and Enterprise plans, and a company admin has to install it.
news.why: Even if you run a small workshop, the idea is useful: AI can turn messy production notes into quotes and reports. Engineering students should learn how AI fits into shop-floor work.

tip.title: Explain a scam video to your parents in Hindi
tip.body: Scams often target parents and grandparents. Ask AI to write a short, kind WhatsApp message in Hindi that explains how fake investment videos work and what to do.
tip.prompt: Write a short WhatsApp message in simple Hindi for my [parents/grandparents]. Explain that AI can make fake videos of famous people like [name of a celebrity or minister] promising high returns. Give 4 easy warning signs, tell them never to click links in such ads, and remind them to call 1930 if money is lost. Keep it warm, under 120 words, no scary language.

title: ChatGPT Retires Old Voice Modes, UP AI Hackathon and More
summary: Today's AI news in simple words: ChatGPT moves everyone to its new voice, a UP AI hackathon for students, Google's DNA AI and a Gemini home update.
intro: Happy Friday! Today we have a big change in how ChatGPT talks to you, a hackathon with cash prizes for UP students, and two Google updates explained simply.

news.headline: ChatGPT will switch off its old voice modes on December 11
news.body: OpenAI is removing the Advanced and Standard voice options from ChatGPT on December 11, 2026. Everyone using them will move to the newer Live voice, powered by GPT-Live, which OpenAI launched in July. The big difference: GPT-Live can listen and talk at the same time, so it feels more like a real phone call. The older voices waited for you to finish speaking first. Your old voice chats will stay in your history, and you can continue them by typing or speaking. Live video and screen-sharing will stay on the old Advanced voice until GPT-Live supports them.
news.why: If you practise spoken English or mock interviews with ChatGPT voice, try the new Live voice now so the switch does not surprise you. Interrupting it mid-answer is now normal, so use that to ask quick follow-ups.

news.headline: UP launches AI Kaushal Hackathon 2026 with Rs 1 lakh prizes
news.body: The Uttar Pradesh government and InMobi have launched the AI Kaushal Hackathon 2026, with IIIT Lucknow as the academic partner. Students, startups and professionals based in UP can register until November 20. Teams first submit an AI use case. Shortlisted teams get mentoring from experts, then build their idea in a 24-hour on-site round at IIIT Lucknow on December 8-9. The top five teams will each win Rs 1 lakh. The best prototypes may also be tested with UP government departments and industry partners.
news.why: For students in UP, this is a real chance to build a portfolio project, meet mentors and maybe win prize money. Even if you are not in UP, it shows that solving a local problem with AI is a strong way to get noticed.

news.headline: Google DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 reads DNA to study disease
news.body: Google DeepMind has released AlphaGenome 2, an AI model that predicts how small changes in our DNA affect what happens inside cells. It was trained on more than 100 million single-cell profiles from 68 types of body tissue. In one test on immune cells, it found the change actually causing an effect 30% of the time, up from 16% for the earlier version. It is only for non-commercial research for now and is not meant for diagnosing patients.
news.why: This is not a tool for everyday users, but it shows where AI careers are growing: biology, health research and data science. Biotech and life-science students can start learning basic Python and data skills to join this field.

news.headline: Gemini for Home gets faster timers and picture answers on smart displays
news.body: Google has released a new update for Gemini for Home, the assistant that is replacing Google Assistant on Nest speakers and displays. It makes smart home controls better and sets, checks and cancels timers and alarms faster. Smart displays like the Nest Hub can now show images with answers, and broadcasts to other speakers play faster. Older Nest cameras also get fixes. For now the update is only for people in Google's early access programme, and Google has not shared a wider rollout date.
news.why: If your family or shop uses a Nest speaker or Nest Hub, these changes will reach you later. For small shops, quick voice timers and alarms are a simple, free way to manage daily tasks hands-free.

tip.title: Turn a local problem into a hackathon idea
tip.body: Hackathon judges love ideas that solve a real problem near you. Use this prompt to turn something you see every day into a clear AI project plan you can submit.
tip.prompt: I am a [year/branch] student in [city]. Help me turn this local problem into an AI hackathon idea: [describe the problem, e.g. long queues at the ration shop]. Give me: 1) a one-line project title, 2) who it helps, 3) how AI solves it in simple steps, 4) free tools I can use to build a basic demo in 24 hours, and 5) a 3-sentence pitch for judges.

title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Carbon, Better Hindi Voice Typing and More
summary: Today's AI news in simple words: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon arrives, ElevenLabs improves Hindi speech-to-text, and Gemini shows what it remembers.
intro: Good morning! Today we look at Google's most powerful new model, better AI transcription for Hindi speakers, and a new way to check what an AI remembers about you.

news.headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon, its most powerful model so far
news.body: Google has released Gemini 4 Carbon, a new top model that sits above Gemini 4 Argon. Google says Carbon is meant for the hardest jobs: long coding tasks, finding bugs, scientific research, and detailed work like reports and spreadsheets. It takes more time and checks its own work before answering. In the Gemini app, Carbon is only for Google AI Ultra subscribers for now, while Argon stays available on AI Pro and higher plans. Developers can use it through the paid Gemini API at a lower introductory price until 30 November.
news.why: Most students and small businesses do not need Carbon for daily tasks. The free and cheaper Gemini models are still fine for notes, emails and study help.

news.headline: ElevenLabs' new speech-to-text gets much better at Hindi
news.body: ElevenLabs, a popular AI voice company, has launched Scribe v3 and Scribe v3 Live. These tools turn speech into written text. The company says Scribe v3 makes 27% fewer word mistakes than the older version across 102 languages, and the Live version makes 43% fewer mistakes. It can also label who is speaking in a meeting. ElevenLabs says Indian customers asked for Hindi to be as good as English, even when people mix languages mid-sentence, and the Live model improved Hindi accuracy by 36%. It also offers data storage inside India for business customers.
news.why: Better Hinglish transcription helps students record lectures, and helps call centres and shops that talk to customers in mixed Hindi and English.

news.headline: Gemini now shows a 'Memory summary' of what it knows about you
news.body: Google is rolling out a new Memory summary in the Gemini app. It is one page where you can see, edit and delete the things Gemini has learned about you from past chats. The details are grouped into sections like work projects, travel, entertainment and fitness. You can add or remove facts by typing, and there is a history view of changes. For now it is only for paid Google AI subscribers using US English on the web, so most Indian users will need to wait.
news.why: It is a good reminder to check what any AI app remembers about you. Avoid sharing passwords, Aadhaar or bank details in AI chats.

tip.title: Turn a Hinglish voice note into clean notes
tip.body: Record your lecture or meeting, get a transcript from any speech-to-text app, then paste it into ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude with this prompt.
tip.prompt: Here is a transcript of a [lecture/meeting] in mixed Hindi and English: [paste transcript]. Please fix spelling mistakes, write clear notes in simple English with headings, list [5] key points, and add a short Hindi summary at the end.

title: Gemini Can Now Book Rides in India, ChatGPT Business Profiles and More
summary: Today's AI news in simple words: Gemini app tasks expand to India, ChatGPT launches business profiles, and Claude gets Sheets and Whiteboards.
intro: Good morning! Today's news is all about AI doing real work for you: booking rides, answering questions about shops, and building spreadsheets.

news.headline: Gemini's task automation is expanding to India
news.body: Google's November update for Android brings more 'Gemini Intelligence' features. The biggest one for us: task automation is expanding to India, the UK and Japan. This means you can ask Gemini to do a job across your apps, like ordering food, booking a cab or making a reservation, instead of tapping through each app yourself. For now it works on supported phones such as the Pixel 10 series and select new Samsung and Motorola models. Google says it is for users aged 18 and above, in select languages, and heavy use may need a subscription.
news.why: If you have a supported phone, you can save time on daily errands. Always check the final order or booking before you confirm payment.

news.headline: ChatGPT launches business profiles, a bit like Google Business Profile
news.body: OpenAI has started a new 'Business Hub' in beta. Companies can create a verified business profile and keep details about their products and services up to date, so ChatGPT gives correct answers when people ask about them. Some eligible businesses can also set up a special business agent that answers customer questions inside ChatGPT. The hub shows simple numbers like profile views, mentions and website clicks. OpenAI has not yet shared full details on eligibility, pricing or which countries get it first.
news.why: More people now search for shops and services by asking ChatGPT. Small businesses in India should watch for this and keep their website and online details accurate.

news.headline: Claude gets Sheets, Whiteboards and a meeting helper
news.body: Anthropic has added new office-style tools to Claude. Claude Sheets lets you build and edit spreadsheets with Claude, including tabs, formulas and dropdowns, and it lists every change it makes. Claude Whiteboards is a shared board for planning timelines and ideas, which can be turned into a doc or slides. Claude Meetings, for Team and Enterprise plans, can join a Google Meet call, take notes and draft action items. Sheets and Whiteboards are in beta on paid plans for web, desktop and mobile.
news.why: AI is moving from just chatting to making real work files. Learning to plan, track and present work with AI tools is a useful skill for any job seeker.

tip.title: Make a simple monthly home budget with AI
tip.body: AI tools can now build spreadsheets for you. Use this prompt in any AI chat to get a ready budget table you can copy into Google Sheets or Excel.
tip.prompt: Make a simple monthly budget table for a family in [city] with a total income of Rs [amount]. Include rows for rent, groceries, electricity, mobile and internet, travel, school or college fees, EMI, savings and emergency fund. Add columns for Planned, Actual and Difference, with a formula for Difference. Then give me 3 easy tips to save money, in [English/Hinglish].

title: Claude Fable 5.2 Launches, Nasscom Warns Freshers and More
summary: Today's AI news in simple words: Anthropic's new Claude Fable 5.2 model, Nasscom's warning for engineering freshers, and Claude's new money tool.
intro: Good morning! Today we explain Anthropic's newest Claude model, what India's IT industry body is saying about jobs for freshers, and a new Claude tool that reads bank accounts, with a simple safety lesson for everyone.

news.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.2, its most powerful public model
news.body: On 9 November, Anthropic released two new models: Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2. Both are built on the same base model. Fable 5.2 is for the public and has safety blocks for risky hacking and biology tasks. Mythos 5.2 has fewer limits, so only approved cybersecurity and science researchers can use it. Anthropic says the new models are faster and better at coding, reasoning and reading images than the 5.1 versions. Paid users get Fable 5.2 inside the Claude app, and developers can use it on Claude's platform and big cloud services like AWS, Google Cloud and Azure.
news.why: These are very advanced and costly models made for big technical projects. For daily study or office work, the regular Claude models are usually enough, so do not feel you must pay to try this one.

news.headline: Nasscom chief says AI is making entry-level IT jobs harder to get
news.body: Rajesh Nambiar, president of Nasscom, the body that represents India's IT companies, told Nikkei Asia that fresh engineering graduates could find it harder to get tech jobs. The reason is that AI now does a lot of basic coding and testing work that freshers used to do. Nasscom still expects India's tech sector to have about 6 million direct jobs in FY26, a small rise of about 2.3%. Nambiar said Nasscom is working with the UGC and other agencies on a joint AI curriculum for undergraduate courses, which could take around six months to be approved.
news.why: If you are a student or fresher, basic coding alone may not be enough. Build real projects that use AI tools, learn to check and fix AI-written code, and show this work on your resume and GitHub.
news.source_name: AI Weekly (summary of Nikkei Asia interview)

news.headline: Claude can now read your bank accounts to explain your spending (US only)
news.body: Anthropic has launched a beta tool called Personal Finance inside Claude. Users connect their bank and credit card accounts through a service called Plaid, and then ask questions like where their money went last month. Claude groups spending into categories, spots duplicate charges and surprise fees, and explains terms like APR. Anthropic says the access is read-only, so Claude cannot move or invest money, and these chats are not used to train its models. For now it is only for Pro, Max and Ultra users in the United States.
news.why: This tool is not in India yet. Whenever any app asks to link your bank, read what it can see, and never type OTPs, UPI PINs, card numbers or passwords into any AI chatbot.

tip.title: Make your resume stand out in the AI era
tip.body: Since AI now does a lot of basic coding work, freshers need to show they can build and check real things. Use this prompt in ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude to turn your projects into strong resume points.
tip.prompt: I am a [your degree, e.g. B.Tech CSE] fresher applying for [job role] jobs in India. Here are my projects: [project 1 in 1-2 lines], [project 2 in 1-2 lines]. Rewrite each project as 2 resume bullet points that show the problem, what I built, the tools I used (including any AI tools) and the result. Then suggest one small project I can finish in 2 weeks to show I can use AI tools well and check their output.

title: India Plans Its Own AI Chip in 2 Years, Fake Job Scam Alert and More
summary: Today's AI news in simple words: India aims to build its own AI chip, a study on how AI is helping Indian workers, and how to spot fake AI-era job scams.
intro: Good morning and happy Monday! Today we look at India's plan to make its own AI chip, a new study on how Indian employees are using AI at work, and a safety guide every student and job seeker should read.

news.headline: India wants its own AI chip (GPU) in about 24 months
news.body: AI tools like ChatGPT and Gemini run on powerful chips called GPUs. Today India buys almost all of these from foreign companies. MeitY Secretary S. Krishnan has said India should have a GPU chip of its own, and that the project will take roughly 24 months under the country's next semiconductor push, often called Semicon 2.0. Separately, the IndiaAI Mission has relaxed the rules for data centres that want to rent AI computing power to the government's shared pool, so more Indian companies can join. This pool already offers subsidised computing to startups, MSMEs, researchers and students.
news.why: A home-grown chip and a bigger shared computing pool could make AI cheaper to build in India. Students and small startups working on AI projects can check the IndiaAI portal for subsidised computing.

news.headline: Cognizant study: 97% of Indian employees say AI helps them work faster
news.body: IT company Cognizant surveyed 700 employees and 75 senior leaders across 10 industries in India. Almost all employees, 97%, said AI made them more productive, with an average boost of about 15%. About 74% of Indian employees had finished some AI training, compared with 56% globally. But leaders said only about 36% of staff actually have access to AI tools at work, and many companies have not yet seen lower costs or higher revenue. The study estimates AI-driven productivity could add $28 billion to $84 billion a year to India's GDP in the near term.
news.why: Employers value people who can actually use AI tools well, not just people who have done a course. Practise using AI on real tasks and mention concrete examples in your resume and interviews.

news.headline: Students warned about AI deepfake calls and fake placement drives
news.body: A new safety guide for Indian students and job seekers lists the tricks scammers now use with AI. These include cloned voices of relatives or bank staff, edited videos of well-known people, and fake recruiters. A common trap is a fake placement drive on WhatsApp or Telegram that asks for a refundable security deposit, sells offer letters or pays you for small tasks before asking for money. The advice: never share your OTP, UPI PIN or passwords, never install unknown APK files, and remember that caller ID and logos can be faked. If money is lost, act fast and report it at 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in.
news.why: Real companies never ask you to pay for a job or an interview. If an offer feels urgent or asks for money, stop, check the company's official website, and talk to someone you trust.

tip.title: Check if a job offer is a scam with AI
tip.body: Inspired by today's scam warning: before you reply to any job message on WhatsApp, Telegram or email, paste it into a chatbot and ask it to look for red flags. Remove your phone number, address and any personal details first.
tip.prompt: I received this job offer message: [paste the message, with my personal details removed]. Act as a careful career advisor in India. List any red flags that suggest it could be a scam (for example payment requests, urgency, unofficial email IDs). Tell me 3 steps to verify if the company and recruiter are real. Explain in simple English and also in Hinglish.

title: Gemini Omni Now Makes 15-Second Videos, 89% of Young Indians Want AI
summary: Today's AI news in simple words: Google's video AI makes longer clips, a report on young Indians and AI, and a lesson after Claude deleted a professor's files.
intro: Happy Sunday! Today we look at Google's upgraded video AI, a new report on how young Indians want to use AI, and one simple habit that can save your files when you let AI work on them.

news.headline: Google's Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash can now make 15-second AI videos
news.body: Google has made its video model Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generally available. It can now create clips up to 15 seconds long, up from 10 seconds in the earlier preview. You can also edit a clip by chatting, for example asking it to change the background, swap a product or fix the lighting, instead of starting again. It is rolling out in Google Vids, Flow and Google Ads, and in the Gemini app for Google AI Ultra subscribers. For developers, the price drops by about 30% to roughly $0.07 per second of 720p video. Every video carries an invisible SynthID watermark.
news.why: Small businesses can make short product clips or reels without a camera crew. Check what your Google account or plan includes before paying for anything, and always label AI-made videos honestly.

news.headline: Report: 89% of young Indians want to use AI for study or work within a year
news.body: A new report from Ayre Think Tank, shared by news agency IANS on 5 November, looks at AI and young people across 56 Commonwealth countries. It says nearly 89% of young Indians want to use AI for education or work within the next year, and more than 60% feel confident using it. India has about 382 million people aged 15 to 29. The report estimates AI could add around $79 billion to India's GDP over ten years. It also warns that about 30% of young people are not in work, education or training, and asks for cheaper access, local-language tools and skills linked to real jobs.
news.why: Most of your classmates and job competitors plan to use AI soon. Learning to use it well, and showing that skill on your resume, can help you stand out.

news.headline: Claude deleted a professor's lecture notes, and a backup saved him
news.body: William Baude, a law professor at the University of Chicago, asked Anthropic's Claude to simply update page numbers in his old lecture notes. He left it running and went for lunch. When he came back, the AI had deleted his current syllabus and a full year of lecture notes. Claude then admitted the mistake and apologised. Luckily, Baude got his files back from Dropbox, which keeps older copies of files. The story spread widely this week as a warning about letting AI tools change files on their own.
news.why: If you let any AI tool edit your assignments, project files or business records, keep a backup copy first, for example in Google Drive or OneDrive, and check its work before you trust it.

tip.title: Plan a 15-second product video with AI
tip.body: Inspired by today's Gemini Omni story: before you make any AI or phone video for your shop or side business, ask a chatbot to plan it shot by shot. A clear plan gives much better results.
tip.prompt: I run a small [type of business, e.g. home bakery / mobile repair shop] in [city]. Write a plan for a 15-second Instagram reel to promote [product or offer]. Split it into 3-4 short shots with timing, what the viewer sees, and one line of on-screen text for each. Add a simple caption in English and in Hinglish, and 5 hashtags. Keep it honest, no fake claims.

title: Gemini Notebook Flashcards Get Images, Dreambeans Comes to India
summary: Today's AI news in simple words: Gemini Notebook flashcards get images and a timer, Google Dreambeans arrives in India, and Claude speeds up a lab study.
intro: Good morning! Today we have a handy study upgrade, a new Google app that speaks Indian languages, and a real science story with an honest lesson about AI mistakes.

news.headline: Gemini Notebook flashcards now support images, a stopwatch and study reminders
news.body: Gemini Notebook can already turn your notes, PDFs and other sources into flashcards automatically. On 6 November, Google added three upgrades. First, cards can now show images, so diagrams and photos can be part of what you revise. Second, there is an optional stopwatch to time how fast you recall each answer. Third, the Android and iOS apps can now send study reminders so you do not skip revision. Google has not clearly said which plans get these first, so open the app and check your flashcards section.
news.why: Picture-based cards are great for biology diagrams, maps and maths figures, and timed recall is good practice for speed-based exams like JEE, NEET or bank and SSC tests.

news.headline: Google's Dreambeans app launches in India with Hindi and 12 more Indian languages
news.body: Dreambeans is an experimental app from Google Labs. Each morning it makes a few short, illustrated stories based on things in your connected Google apps, such as Calendar, Gmail, Photos, Search and YouTube. You do not need to type a prompt. India is the first country outside the US to get it. It works on Android and iOS, in English plus 13 Indian languages including Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Bengali and Marathi, but one language at a time. You need a personal Google account and must be 18 or older. You choose which apps to connect and can delete your data.
news.why: It shows big AI companies are now building for Indian-language users first. Before you connect Gmail or Photos to any AI app, think about what personal data you are comfortable sharing.

news.headline: Claude helps scientists map a tiny virus structure, but also makes mistakes
news.body: Anthropic's biology team used its Claude AI to help build the first 3D picture of a 'vault particle', a hollow, barrel-like structure, from a virus that infects bacteria. Claude cut one lab step from about three days to 90 minutes. But it also got things wrong: one bad suggestion for a lab additive delayed the work by two weeks, and it made a mirror-image error in a map. The results are shared as a preprint, which means other experts have not reviewed them yet.
news.why: AI can save huge time in research and projects, but you still need to check its work. For students doing lab work or final-year projects, treat AI as a fast helper, not the final judge.

tip.title: Turn any chapter into smart flashcards
tip.body: Use this with Gemini Notebook, ChatGPT or Claude to make exam-ready flashcards from your own notes. Ask for picture ideas too, so you can add diagrams to the cards.
tip.prompt: Here are my notes on [chapter/topic] for [exam name, e.g. NEET / Class 12 boards]: [paste notes]. Make 15 flashcards. Each card should have a short question on the front and a 1-2 line answer on the back. Mark 5 of them as 'hard'. For any card where a diagram would help, suggest what picture I should add. Finally, give me a 7-day revision schedule using these cards, 20 minutes a day.

title: ChatGPT Can Now Make GIFs, AI Job Hiring Jumps 32% and More
summary: Today's AI news in simple words: ChatGPT now turns photos into GIFs, Naukri says AI/ML hiring is up 32%, and India warns banks about AI-powered cyber attacks.
intro: Three AI updates for your Friday: a fun new ChatGPT feature anyone can try, good news for AI job seekers, and a safety warning from India's cybercrime agency.

news.headline: ChatGPT can now turn your photos and ideas into animated GIFs
news.body: OpenAI has rolled out a new image update called Images 2.6 in ChatGPT. The biggest change: you can now ask for a short animated GIF. Type an idea, like a dancing cat, or upload a photo and ask ChatGPT to animate it. You can change how fast the animation plays and edit single frames. OpenAI also says image making is quicker overall. The update is reaching all ChatGPT users on web, desktop and mobile, including the free plan. OpenAI says people now make more than four billion images a week with its tools.
news.why: Small shops and creators can make simple moving greetings, offer posts and WhatsApp stickers for free, without learning any design software.

news.headline: Naukri JobSpeak: AI and machine learning hiring up 32% in October
news.body: Naukri's JobSpeak report for October 2026, released on 3 November, shows white-collar hiring in India grew 14% compared to last year. AI and machine learning roles grew much faster, by 32%. Hyderabad led among cities with 15% growth, followed by Pune and Delhi-NCR. Plain software and testing jobs grew only about 1%. Skills showing up often in AI job posts include GenAI, RAG, vector databases and MLOps. For freshers, entry roles in data operations, QA automation, analyst internships and platform support are said to be the easier way in.
news.why: If you are job hunting, learning to use and build with AI tools is now one of the clearest ways to stand out, even for non-AI roles.

news.headline: India's cybercrime agency warns banks about AI-powered attacks
news.body: The Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C), under the Home Ministry, has warned banks, fintech apps and payment companies that criminals are now using AI agents to break into systems very quickly. CERT-In has also issued related alerts. The warning came days after microfinance lender Spandana Sphoorty reported that nearly Rs 7.8 crore was moved out of one of its bank accounts without permission on 1 November. The advisory asks companies to set transaction limits, check who money is going to, and report attacks within six hours.
news.why: Scammers are getting faster with AI. Never share OTPs or click unknown payment links, and if you lose money, call 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in right away.

tip.title: Find the AI skills your dream job wants
tip.body: AI jobs are growing fast, but every job post asks for different skills. Paste a real job post into ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude and get a simple learning plan plus resume lines you can honestly use.
tip.prompt: Here is a job post I want to apply for: [paste job post]. My current skills are: [your skills]. 1) List the top 5 skills this job wants, in simple words. 2) Tell me which ones I already have and which I am missing. 3) Give me a 30-day free learning plan for the missing ones, 1 hour a day. 4) Suggest 3 resume bullet points I can use once I finish, without adding anything fake.

title: IndiaAI Launches EKA-1 and Dhir AI Models, WhatsApp AI Chats and More
summary: Today's AI news in simple words: IndiaAI releases 3 homegrown AI models, WhatsApp tests separate Meta AI chats, Guided Learning comes to Google Classroom.
intro: Three AI updates for today: India's own new AI models, a handy change coming to Meta AI on WhatsApp, and a Gemini study mode that teachers can now add to homework.

news.headline: IndiaAI Mission releases three homegrown AI models: EKA-1, Dhir 2B and Dhir 5B
news.body: On 3 November in New Delhi, MeitY and the IndiaAI Mission unveiled three AI models built in India. EKA-1, from Soket AI Labs, has about 26 billion parameters and covers all 22 scheduled Indian languages plus English. It is meant for maths, coding and reasoning, and for banks that need AI on their own servers, even offline. Dhir 2B and Dhir 5B, from ZenteiQ AiTech, are small models for English and 10 Indian languages. They are built for document search, and can run on a mobile phone offline. Access is through the government's AIKosh platform; Soket says EKA-1's weights will open up within about a month via a waitlist.
news.why: India now has its own AI models that understand Indian languages and can work without internet. Students and developers can try them through AIKosh, and skills in Indian-language AI are becoming a real job area.

news.headline: WhatsApp is testing separate Meta AI chats you can name
news.body: WhatsApp is rolling out a new option to some Android beta testers (version 2.26.44.6). Instead of one long Meta AI conversation, you can start separate Meta AI chats from the menu, give each one a name and even a picture. Each chat keeps its own context, so what you discuss in one does not mix into another. These chats sit in your normal chat list, and a new optional 'AI' filter helps you find them. You can delete them any time. WhatsApp has not said when everyone will get it, so it may take a few weeks to reach regular users.
news.why: If you use Meta AI on WhatsApp, you will soon be able to keep one chat for exam doubts, one for shop replies and one for trip plans, without them getting mixed up.

news.headline: Teachers can now add Gemini's Guided Learning to Google Classroom homework
news.body: Google says teachers can now attach a Guided Learning activity to any assignment in Google Classroom. Guided Learning is a Gemini mode that explains a topic step by step and asks questions, instead of just giving the final answer. Teachers can choose class materials for it to use, see short AI summaries of how the class and each student did, and read student chats. It is rolling out globally from 3 November, in all Gemini-supported languages, for schools on Google Workspace for Education editions, but only where the school admin has switched Gemini on.
news.why: If your school or college uses Google Classroom, you may soon get homework where AI coaches you instead of doing it for you. You can already use Guided Learning yourself in the Gemini app to understand tough chapters.

tip.title: Make AI teach you, not just answer
tip.body: Inspired by today's Guided Learning story: before an exam, ask any AI chatbot to quiz you step by step instead of giving the answers. You learn faster when you try first.
tip.prompt: I am preparing for [exam name, e.g. Class 12 boards / AKTU / SSC]. Teach me [topic] step by step like a patient tutor. Do not give me the full answer at once. Ask me one question at a time, wait for my reply, tell me if I am right, and explain my mistakes in simple English. Start with an easy question and make them harder. After 5 questions, give me a short summary of what I should revise.

title: ChatGPT Lets You Lock Chats With a PIN, Deepfake Curbs and More
summary: Today's AI news in simple words: ChatGPT can lock private chats, Centre promises deepfake curbs, an Indian voice AI speaks 14 languages, Gemini AI Plus changes.
intro: Four quick AI updates for today: a new privacy feature in ChatGPT, the government's latest word on deepfakes, a Bengaluru startup's multilingual voice AI, and a plan change some Gemini users should know about.

news.headline: ChatGPT now lets you lock private chats behind a PIN
news.body: OpenAI is slowly rolling out a feature called Locked Chats, including for Free and Go users. You can lock any single chat with a four-digit PIN, or with Face ID, fingerprint or your phone unlock on supported devices. Locked chats move into a separate 'Locked chats' area and stop showing in your normal history and search. It works on the web, the phone apps and the new desktop apps. Two warnings: if you forget the PIN and reset it, the locked chats are deleted for good, and locking a chat removes it from any project it was in.
news.why: If you share a phone or laptop with family, you can keep chats about your resume, salary talks or business plans private. Write your PIN somewhere safe, because a reset wipes those chats.

news.headline: Amit Shah promises stronger action against AI deepfakes
news.body: On 2 November, Union Home Minister Amit Shah met actors Chiranjeevi and Ram Charan in Hyderabad, who raised concerns about AI deepfakes being used against artists. Shah said the government will urgently look into the problem, with stronger safeguards and strict penalties, and asked the film industry to send a written representation. Separately, IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw has said a consultation paper on AI rules, covering safety and deepfakes, is due in the coming weeks. It is not out yet.
news.why: Fake videos and voice clones are already used in scams. Until new rules arrive, protect yourself: if a 'family member' or 'officer' asks for urgent money on a call or video, hang up and call them back on a number you know. Report fraud on 1930.

news.headline: Bengaluru startup Arrowhead launches Fletch, a voice AI for 14 languages
news.body: Arrowhead AI has launched Fletch, its own text-to-speech model built for customer calls in India and Southeast Asia. It covers 14 languages, including Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Bengali and English, and can switch languages in the middle of a sentence, the way many Indians speak. The company says it starts speaking in under 100 milliseconds and already handles over a million calls a day for clients such as banks and lenders. The accuracy claims come from the company itself.
news.why: The next call from your bank or loan app may be an AI voice in your own language. For job seekers, this shows rising demand for people who can build, test and train AI in Indian languages.

news.headline: Gemini AI Plus users lose Pro models from 13 November
news.body: Google has been emailing people on its lower-priced Gemini AI Plus plan to say that Pro models will no longer be part of that plan from 13 November 2026. After that, Pro models in the Gemini app and in AI Mode will need Google AI Pro or a higher plan. AI Plus will keep the Flash and Flash-Lite models, and old chats that used Pro can carry on with another model. The free plan continues.
news.why: If you pay for AI Plus mainly for Pro answers, check your plan before you renew. For most study notes, emails and everyday questions, the Flash models or the free plan may be enough.

tip.title: Write customer replies in Hinglish
tip.body: Inspired by today's multilingual voice AI story: small shop owners can use any free AI chatbot to write friendly WhatsApp replies in the language their customers actually use. Read it once before sending and fix prices or dates yourself.
tip.prompt: I run a small [type of business] in [city]. A customer sent this message: "[paste customer message]". Write 3 short, polite WhatsApp replies in simple Hinglish (Hindi in English letters). Mention [price/offer/timing] clearly. Keep each reply under 50 words and end with a friendly line asking them to visit or order.

title: Gemini Now Edits PDFs in Chat, IndiaAI Fellowship Deadline and More
summary: Today's AI news in simple words: Gemini can now create and edit PDFs and docs inside chat, IndiaAI Fellowship closes 30 Nov, and Bihar pushes AI in schools.
intro: Three AI updates worth your two minutes today: a handy new Gemini feature for notes and assignments, a paid fellowship Indian AI students should not miss, and a state government telling school staff to start using AI.

news.headline: Gemini can now create and edit PDFs, docs and slides right inside the chat
news.body: Google has added a way to make a file in Gemini and then keep working on it without leaving the conversation. You can, for example, upload photos of handwritten notes and ask for a PDF study guide, see it previewed in the chat, open it full screen, edit it yourself, or highlight one part and ask Gemini to rewrite it. Google says it works wherever the Gemini app is available. PDFs work on phone and web; Google Docs, Sheets, slides and text or code files are web only for now.
news.why: Students can turn class notes into a clean revision PDF in minutes, and small businesses can draft a price list or flyer and fix it line by line instead of starting again each time.

news.headline: IndiaAI Fellowship 2026: applications close 30 November
news.body: The IndiaAI Fellowship under MeitY's IndiaAI Mission supports full-time UG, PG and PhD students in India working on AI. Reported support goes up to ₹1 lakh for undergraduates and ₹2 lakh for postgraduates, with monthly support for eligible PhD scholars. Undergraduates usually need a few AI-related courses to qualify. Reports say there is no application fee, so ignore anyone asking for money to 'guarantee' a seat.
news.why: If you are a B.Tech or MCA student taking AI or ML subjects, this is real money for your project. Read the official notice on fellowship.indiaai.gov.in, get your HoD's signature early, and apply well before the last day.

news.headline: Bihar asks school education staff to use ChatGPT, Claude and other AI tools
news.body: On 2 November, Bihar's Education Department wrote to all District Education Officers asking them to encourage officials and staff in government schools and education offices to use AI apps such as ChatGPT and Claude. The suggested uses are office work: reviewing schemes, organising data and cutting down routine paperwork. It is encouragement, not a strict order, and no training plan was mentioned.
news.why: AI skills are moving from 'nice to have' to expected, even in government offices. Learning to use these tools well now gives you an edge in almost any job.

tip.title: Turn messy notes into a revision sheet
tip.body: Take a clear photo of your handwritten notes, upload it to Gemini, ChatGPT or Claude, and paste this prompt. Always check the answer against your textbook before you trust it.
tip.prompt: These are my class notes on [topic] for my [subject] exam. Turn them into a one-page revision sheet: 5 key points, 3 important definitions, 1 simple diagram described in words, and 5 likely exam questions with short answers. Mark anything in my notes that looks wrong or unclear.
